title: minutia.v1
description: The canonical minutia record of the dactyloscopy repository, frozen as a JSON Schema before any reader or writer exists. Every numeric field is an integer: two implementations must agree on values exactly, with no tolerance. Decisions in quality/REF-008-minutia-canon-format.md; the facts they rest on are named in x-manifest.rests_on.

canon.description: The format this file claims to be. Frozen for the life of v1.

image.description: The image the minutiae were extracted from, populated from the dataset manifest and never from a tool's output (REF-007 decision 1). This is the block that is read.

dataset.description: Dataset manifest id, <competition>/<subset>. Never a path.

id.description: The image's identifier within that dataset. The identifier space belongs to the dataset manifest, not to this format.

produced_by.description: The tool that produced these minutiae, and the properties of its output that a reader needs in order to check its own arithmetic.

tool.description: Tool and release, as <name>@<release>. A tool that reports no version of its own is identified by binary_sha256; the release names the artefact it was built from.

binary_sha256.description: Digest of the binary as it sat in the image that produced this file.

invocation.description: The command form, including every flag. A run that does not name the invocation has not named the tool (REF-005).

read_from.description: Which of the tool's output files this record was built from. Deliberately not an enumeration: a source this format does not yet know of must not require a new schema version.

angle_levels.description: The source's own angular quantisation: how many distinct directions it can express in a full circle. A fact about the source, not about the canon. It exists so that a reader's angle arithmetic can be checked against the grid the source actually used.

conventions.description: The canon's own conventions, stated by every file rather than assumed by every reader. All five are constant for the life of v1: a file that needs different conventions is a different format.

angle_direction.description: The direction the angle points, named by the standard that defines it. What that direction is in absolute terms is an open question, tracked as D-3 (issue 7); how it relates to the native NBIS direction is D-4 (issue 8). The label is frozen here; its meaning is not settled by this manifest.

minutiae.description: A sequence in the source's order, not a set. Order is meaningful and nothing may sort it: two byte-exact round trips are the only external tests a reader and a writer can be held to (REF-006 decision 3). JSON Schema cannot express that the order carries meaning; uniqueItems is deliberately absent, and two identical entries are legal.

x.description: Pixel column, origin top-left. That x is inside the image is an invariant this schema cannot express: see x-manifest.invariants.

y.description: Pixel row, origin top-left. Same limitation as x.

angle.description: Direction in units of 1/32 degree, on [0, 11519]. That the value lies on the source's own grid is checked below for the quantisations this format knows; for any other value of angle_levels it is not expressible.

type.description: unknown is distinct from other: a tool that does not report the type is not reporting that the type is other.

quality.description: Observed, never derived from reliability. Absent-as-null is not permitted; the field is required.

reliability.description: Present only when the source provides it, and then observed, never derived from quality. When the source provides none the key is absent; null is not a permitted value, which this schema does enforce.

source_header.description: What the source file carried that this format cannot reconstruct from its own fields. Preserved verbatim so that a byte-exact regeneration of the source remains possible, and never read as data (REF-007 decision 3). An empty object is the correct value for a source with no header. Its contents are constrained only in that no floating-point number may appear anywhere inside it.

allOf.$comment: Invariant 1, for the quantisations this format knows: angle lies on the source's own grid, step = 11520 / angle_levels. mindtct native.
ANSI INCITS 378-2004 as written by FingerJetFXOSE: 180 levels, step 64.
ISO/IEC 19794-2:2005 as written by FingerJetFXOSE: 256 levels, step 45.

integerOnlyValue.description: Any JSON value that contains no floating-point number at any depth. Used for source_header, where the contents are opaque but the no-float rule still holds.

x-manifest.$comment: Not a JSON Schema keyword. Unrecognised keywords are ignored by a validator, so this block travels with the schema without changing what it validates. It exists because manifests/README.md requires that every number in a manifest carry a status, and a JSON Schema cannot carry one inside its own keywords.
x-manifest.directory_contract: manifests/README.md requires a manifest to name the INVs and REFs that produced it, to be immutable and versioned, and to give every number a status. The first two are met above. The third needed a reading, which REF-008 records: the four-status vocabulary governs values this repository asserts about the world, and a schema also contains bounds that assert nothing. Both kinds are enumerated below; the asserted ones carry a status and the structural ones are named as structural rather than given one.

angle_full_circle.note: 1/32 degree is the smallest unit in which the native, ANSI 378 and ISO 19794-2 angular grids are all whole numbers, so a full circle is 360 * 32. INV-002 F-16.

angle_maximum.note: angle_full_circle - 1. The circle is closed, so 11520 is the same direction as 0 and only one of the two spellings is legal.

angle_levels_native_step.note: 11520 / 32. mindtct exposes 32 distinct directions: INV-002 F-6 measured 32 distinct direction indices over 3946 minutiae, and INV-004 confirmed NUM_DIRECTIONS 16 with a half-circle unit of 180/16 degrees in the source.

angle_levels_ansi_step.note: 11520 / 180. ANSI INCITS 378-2004 as written by FingerJetFXOSE carries 180 levels of 2 degrees: INV-003 F-1, arithmetic on the serializer confirmed at the pinned commit.

angle_levels_iso_step.note: 11520 / 256. ISO/IEC 19794-2:2005 as written by FingerJetFXOSE carries 256 levels of 360/256 degrees: INV-003 F-1. What the standard's own text defines is not established here and is tracked as D-3, issue 7.

angle_levels_maximum.note: A source cannot express more distinct directions than the canon has units. Equal to angle_full_circle for the same reason.

quality_maximum.note: The canon's declared scale, taken from the scale the sources use. Over the 3946 minutiae of one corpus the observed range was 1 to 99 with no value outside 0 to 100 (INV-002 F-9), and FingerJetFXOSE clamps its own quality at 100 (INV-003 S-6). Observing a range is not the same as knowing one; the declared scale is what a reader enforces, and a value outside it is a defect to raise rather than clamp.

reliability_maximum.note: The canon's declared scale. mindtct prints its reliability as a value on [0,1] with exactly three decimals (INV-002 F-9, and INV-004 confirms the %6.3f format in the source), so 1/1000 is the exact integer image of what the source states, with no rounding introduced by the canon.

structural_numbers.$comment: Bounds that assert nothing about the world. They are the format's own definition, and the four-status vocabulary does not apply to them.
structural_numbers.minimum_0_for_x_y_angle_quality_reliabil: Zero is the least value each of these five fields may take. A negative coordinate, angle, quality or reliability has no meaning in this format.
structural_numbers.minimum_1_for_width_height_resolution_dp: An image with a zero dimension or a zero resolution is not an image.
structural_numbers.minimum_1_for_angle_levels: A source expresses at least one direction.
structural_numbers.minItems_1_for_read_from: A record was built from at least one source file.
structural_numbers.minItems_0_for_minutiae: An image on which the extractor found nothing yields a valid record with zero minutiae, which is a designed value and not an error (REF-006).
structural_numbers.minLength_1_for_strings: An empty string is not an identifier, a tool name or a command.
structural_numbers.length_64_in_binary_sha256_pattern: The hexadecimal length of a SHA-256 digest.

enforced_by_this_schema: Every numeric field is an integer, including at every depth inside source_header.
x, y, quality and reliability are non-negative, and quality and reliability lie within their declared scales.
type is one of exactly four values, and unknown is distinct from other.
reliability is absent rather than null when the source provides none: the key is not required, its type is integer, and null therefore fails.
No property outside this schema may appear, at any level: additionalProperties is false throughout except inside source_header.
The five conventions are constants, so a file cannot silently declare a different scale.
Invariant 1 (angle on the source's grid) for angle_levels of 32, 180 and 256, by conditional subschemas: step 360, 64 and 45 respectively.

not_expressible_in_json_schema.invariant: angle % (11520 / angle_levels) == 0 for an arbitrary angle_levels
not_expressible_in_json_schema.why: JSON Schema has no arithmetic between two instance locations. The conditional subschemas above cover the three quantisations this format knows; a fourth source would validate against the bound on angle but not against its own grid.
not_expressible_in_json_schema.enforced_instead: Nowhere yet. This format is frozen before it has a producer, so nothing implements it. REF-008 records the check as a requirement on the first reader and writer, and it is the reason angle_levels is in the record at all.

not_expressible_in_json_schema.why: The bound lives in a different part of the instance from the value it bounds, and JSON Schema cannot compare the two.
not_expressible_in_json_schema.enforced_instead: Nowhere yet, on the same terms. The lower bound is enforced above; only the upper bound is missing.

not_expressible_in_json_schema.why: Divisibility of a constant by an instance value is not expressible. A source whose quantisation does not divide 11520 cannot be represented on this grid at all, so this is a precondition on a source, not a property of a file.
not_expressible_in_json_schema.enforced_instead: Nowhere yet. A source that fails it needs a new canon version, not a new file.

not_expressible_in_json_schema.invariant: The order of minutiae carries meaning
not_expressible_in_json_schema.why: A JSON array is ordered, so the order survives; that it must not be reordered is a statement about readers and writers, not about instances.
not_expressible_in_json_schema.enforced_instead: By the round-trip test REF-006 decision 3 exists for, once there is something to test.

not_expressible_in_json_schema.why: JSON Schema's integer type tests the value, not the lexical form: 44.0 has a zero fractional part and validates as an integer. This was checked rather than assumed, and it does validate.
not_expressible_in_json_schema.enforced_instead: By the canonical serialisation below, which writes every integer without a fractional part. A file received from elsewhere may spell an integer as 44.0 and this schema will accept it.

serialisation.$comment: Two different jobs, deliberately not conflated. REF-008 decision 4.

for_addressing.purpose: So that a canon file has a stable digest a run record can point at.
rules: Object keys sorted by Unicode code point at every level.
Indent of exactly two spaces per level.
Line ending LF, and no other line ending anywhere.
Exactly one trailing newline at end of file.
ASCII only: any character outside U+0000..U+007F is escaped.

for_comparing_implementations.purpose: So that two readers written in different languages can be shown to agree.
for_comparing_implementations.rule: The comparison is of parsed content, never of bytes.
for_comparing_implementations.why: A byte comparison fails when someone changes an indent, which is a failure for an uninteresting reason. This repository has already refused that trade once, over the intermediate PNG, whose fidelity is checked on decoded pixels and never on encoded bytes.

validation.validator: python-jsonschema 4.25.1, Draft202012Validator, in a throwaway container
checked: check_schema passes: the file is a valid JSON Schema under draft 2020-12.
A hand-written conforming instance validates with zero errors.

Six further instances that must be accepted are accepted: zero minutiae; reliability absent; a step-64 angle at 180 levels; a step-45 angle at 256 levels; a source_header carrying integers; and a read_from naming a source this format does not know.
Twenty-nine deliberately malformed instances each fail, and each fails on the keyword expected of it.

Five instances that the schema is known not to catch were confirmed to be accepted, so that the list of what is not enforced is measured rather than assumed: x beyond image.width, y beyond image.height, an integer spelled 50.0, an angle_levels that does not divide 11520, and two identical minutiae in the sequence.
The instance used for validation is not committed: it contains a minutia, and this repository never commits one.

not_in_this_file: Any minutia. The example that accompanied the brief for this format was minutia index 2 of FVC2002 101_1, carrying that print's real coordinates, angle, quality and reliability; committing it would have been an incident under the repository's first prohibition. No minutia-shaped record appears in this file, in an examples block or anywhere else.
Any reader, writer, or validation tooling. The format is frozen before it has a producer so that the first implementation conforms to it rather than defining it.
